differences.what: B spells out the row-by-row computation behind B1 (rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-3 change scratch to a+Vx, c+Gx, rows 4-5 add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx), rows 6-7 restore); A states the net change and that rows 0-1 subtract the old contribution, so B1 is present in both
A gives the formula W_c=2N+I(vz_c+c_c) as well as the value; B gives only the value for W_c

items.note: Both plans carry B1-B4 with the correct coefficients, cases and three-stage composition. The differences are in how much detail each gives and balance out.
Both state the invariant, the commutation of a common frame with a pointwise gate, the operator D_out S D_in^{-1} and the route formula including auxiliary roles.

differences.what: B lists the full residual table (every edge class with its orthogonal residual and dimension); A only says to tabulate it and gives the 2->5 and 3->4 rows
A states that over F_2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating, so it has an orthonormal basis; B never establishes that these bases exist

items.note: Each plan has four of the five sub-steps (L2, L3 and L5 in both). B has the residual table (L1) and A has the F_2 orthonormal bases (L4). B also adds a minor wrong gloss to the 0->2 row. The two point in opposite directions and are of similar weight.

differences.what: A defines the shear frame Phi_M:(H,D)->(H+MD,D) with M_v=P_{U_v}; B only names Phi_M later, without its definition
A gives the reason for the N extra ranks (at stage 1 B=0 and the first gate on X_a has label exactly U_a); B states the rank-one edge 2P_{U_a} without it

items.note: Both carry the projections, endpoint identity I_m, the rank of P_V-P_U and the value of s_b. A also has the frame definition and the stage-1 reason for the extra source ranks.

differences.what: A states the phase-difference formula q_V-q_U = sum_v wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal residual basis (negated on decreasing edges); B states only the additivity of weight mod 4 and the odd weights
B gives the endpoint frames (zero label I, full label C^{tensor m} since q_F=wt) and the X_a->Y_a phase difference wt(x)+2[u.x]; A lacks both
A negates the physical X outputs to remove the sign of the scalar exchange; B omits this

items.note: Both have P2, both lack P3, and each covers different parts of P4. A carries the defining formula of P1, which B has only partially, so A is slightly ahead.
Both carry R1-R4: L/N<1/2 with positive deficits, the exact eta_b and eta_c, and the log m<20 comparison giving tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}.

differences.what: A states the elementary stream operations and the controlled cyclic shift lemma (split each fiber at the offset and merge the pieces in opposite order; fixed units and negation in O(V)); B has no step for this item and relies only on page names

items.note: Only A carries the linear-cost building blocks behind the triangular shears and the CRT shifts.

differences.what: A's prime also avoids the diagonal numerators, so the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b; B mentions only denominators
B states how the factorization is applied: transform D by E_2 and H by E_1^{-1}, add Pi D to H, then transform back; A lacks this

items.note: Both have M1, M3 and M4. A has the invertibility detail of M2, and B has the order in which the factorization is applied. The differences are minor and point both ways.

differences.what: A shows that descriptor processing fits the O(V) node term (V_j>=q^{2e_0}, log V_0=O(log 2V_j)); B covers the parking stack but not descriptor work

items.note: Both have the row split, the edge shears, the Phi_{I_m} output, the three shears, s calls, the recurrence and the parking schedule. A adds the descriptor bound of the fixed-tape schedule.
Both carry the same reduction: rho high digits as rows, padding to W^k, base-m pieces with the geometric sum, binary padding to q^e, and unequal widths.

Both have the identities for C and H_0, conjugation by P_M, slots of f chunks, one forward child per inverse kernel, a fixed number of row additions, s_c child calls and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. Small presentational differences balance out.

differences.what: A explains that each rotation uses a width-L chunk swap of cost O(VL^tau), which is where the L^tau term comes from
B handles the omitted top selected position by a two-bit XOR in O(V); A leaves it out

items.note: Both have the parity cycles, the guards, the bad set and its union bound, the permutation T_0S_0^{-1} on the bad set and the repair by radix sort. Each has one extra detail.

Both have q_0, k_0, row padding, the exact 1/W split, the recurrence with leaf cutoff, the internal and leaf sums and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}). A lists the exponent conditions explicitly; B uses them in the bounds and adds the LIFO parking and the restored zero rows.

differences.what: A gives m^10<B<m^11, hence nu=11 and C_1=20; B defines the constants without their values here
A bounds the per-invocation operation count (at most 12W gates, 2W^2 per gate, 4s+4W+4 corrections, total 24W^3+4s+4W+4<E); B states only the recurrence
A verifies the width bands that make every packed child cost O(M R_g (L^tau+1)) uniformly (R_g<=12rp, A_*<=C_A p, extra terms tend to zero); B lacks this part of the proof

items.note: Both have S3-S5. B has S1 and S2 only partially (no nu and C_1 values, no per-invocation bound below E) and lacks the uniformity check of the proposition's proof.

differences.what: A identifies the exact counterparts by conjugation with L: (L D_- L^{-1})L=LBF^- and L^{-1}(L D_+ L^{-1})=F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}; B never derives the LBF^- order that the convolution later relies on
A gives the multi-axis round's monomial exponent E=-sum (2r/u_i) b_i k_i mod 2r and shows each round is a contraction; B describes the grouping without the formula or the contraction
A implements the monomial y^E by split, swap and negation in O(rp) per record, and states the truncation bound for Q_p; B lacks both
B gives the reason that the reverse level composes to I/2 (H_0^2=I/2)

items.note: Both carry character cancellation, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage and the layout cost. Only A derives the exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} and the round structure.

differences.what: A gives the final normalization: right shift by p+l bits, with error below sqrt2 2^{-p}
B gives the four absolute-value products with signs restored and the real and imaginary streams ac-be, ae+bc

items.note: Both have B_0=2^{4p}, the separation bound, the carries and the centered residues, the reduction mod y^r+1 and the four-product cost. Each adds one small detail.
Both have the normalization, the convolution theorem, the commutation of pointwise products with LB, and the error chain 2delta+eta, 3delta+eta, M(3delta+eta) with M products.

differences.what: A defines the Gaussian maps S, T and the near-identity N=CTD (nearest coordinates q_j, weights); B uses S, T and N without defining them
A states the construction A=S', B_0=D'J'C, both contractions; B gives the normalization product but never says what A and B_0 are
A derives the error bounds 16p<p^2 and 4+3p^2/4<p^2 for the composed maps, and the setup per line on the padded box

items.note: Only A gives the defining construction of the contractions A and B_0 from the Gaussian maps. Both carry the identity, the Neumann series, the norms and the tensor interface.

differences.what: A obtains RF_s^+ by complex conjugation of the input and output, F~^+(z)=conj(F~(conj z)), the lemma's final clause; B lacks it

items.note: Both carry the chirp periodicity, the Bluestein coefficient check, the dilation identity RF^+R=F^+ and the (u*v)/S^2 cancellation. A adds the conjugation clause.

differences.what: B states the size relations (Tp=Theta(n), d=Theta(p^eps), ...) with the comparison constants a_d=a_r=1/12, b_d=1, b_r=1/3
A states gamma<=b/4 for b>=2^24 and t_i<=T<2^p

items.note: Both have the fixed exponents, the sizes, alpha, gamma, eta, the Rosser-Schoenfeld prime bound, the Bernoulli estimate T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta>p and the trial-division search. The small extras balance.
Both have the isomorphism via the order of the image of x, the triangular coordinates b_i, the update order d..1, the preserved padding and the cost O(Tp d^2(1+l^tau)).
Both have well-definedness, the diagonal isomorphism, the wrap check zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T and the computed twist sequence.

differences.what: A defines the opposite-sign procedure F~^+(z)=conj(F~(conj z)) with exact counterpart RF_s^+, and the chirp phase numerator mod 2r; B uses F~^+ without defining it

items.note: Both carry the source transform, its exact counterpart RF_s, the six steps and the two scalings by S. A also defines F~^+.

differences.what: A tracks the disk margins that keep every intermediate array a permitted input (norms .51, .701, .501, .26, ||w~||<1/16+10^{-3}); B adds the errors without checking them

items.note: Both carry the error chain E_ring, 6TL, 8TL, E_s, E_w, the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding and the carry invariant. A also checks the conditions under which each contraction step applies.

differences.what: A bounds the exceptional streams of the packed calls by O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})=o(V), and justifies the chirp and packed-product rows; B lacks these

items.note: Both have the seven rows, the margins g_1..g_7, min 2^{-181}=2kappa, the absorption of log factors and the schoolbook cutoff. A also covers the exceptional-address sorting named in the result.
Neither plan states the negation argument (one machine with liminf T/(n lg n)=0). A states the conjecture and the setting, and B asserts the disproof in its root claim.

chain.note: Both follow the paper's route: network, frames, labels, s<Wm with exact deficits, tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, the two recurrences, then interchange and layer costs, transforms, convolution, resampling, assembly and time. A's chain is better supported at three joints. It establishes the F_2 orthonormal bases that the complex interface needs, the stream primitives behind the controlled shifts, and the exact counterparts LBF^- that link the transforms to the convolution. B has the residual table but compresses the complex recurrence's result into O(e^lambda).

errors.says: At a node with e=m^k chunks, the s children plus binary basis changes, scalar gates, endpoint corrections and reassembly cost O(V((eK)^tau+1)) at that node.
errors.paper: The node makes s recursive calls; only the non-recursive work (basis changes, gates, corrections, reassembly) costs O(V((eK)^tau+1)). The children are charged separately as (s/W)F(e/m).

errors.says: The side wire edge 0->2 has residual dimension (a-1)(h-1)+1, using that the two triples are orthogonal.
errors.paper: Only the side edge 2->5 uses the neighbour relation t_X perp t_Y. The other entries, including 0->2, follow directly by splitting A=B perp P and F=<t> perp t^perp.

errors.says: The recurrence solves to O(e^lambda) for the complex network.
errors.paper: The internal nodes sum to O(e^lambda), but the leaves contribute O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and the layer total is O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda'>max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}. B's own child step S0.1.1.1.6.2 states this correctly.

errors.says: Per-node overheads are polynomial in p and absorbed by the length of the polynomial record.
errors.paper: The node overhead is O(V((eK)^tau+1)). Only the descriptor and address work that is polynomial in p per record is absorbed by the Theta(rp) record length.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both carry the central saving (s<Wm, the exact deficits, tau=1-2^{-50}, the recurrences) equally well. A is clearly more complete on three core derivations that B thins out: the guard-width constants and the per-invocation operation bound of the simultaneous layer (S1, S2), the exact counterparts LBF^- of the transform layout, and the construction A=S', B_0=D'J'C of Gaussian resampling. A also has the stream primitives and the F_2 orthonormal bases, which B lacks. B's only advantages are the residual table (L1) and a few small details, which do not offset these.
